1) Pen test access window: we need to coordinate a timeframe in August or September for an external pen test. Can Redwood confirm acceptable windows and any constraints (notice period, blackout periods, staging vs prod)?

2) Evidence cadence & delivery: our auditors will request SOC 2 report, sampled logs (7–14 days), and a short list of configuration screenshots. Can you confirm your preferred evidence cadence and the mechanism (SFTP/Drive/portal) for delivery? Also please indicate SLA for evidence requests (e.g., 3–5 business days).

If you can send a short proposed exhibit redline and a suggested evidence timetable we can review with legal. If easier, cc your legal and security folks and we can do a 30-min sync.

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks and the constraints doc. Looping in Jordan (legal) and Karthik (security) so we can provide a concise exhibit redline and an evidence cadence that lines up with NexaCare's expectations.

High level from our side:
- Pen test notice: we can work with a 30-day notice for external tests and provide a 2-week blackout window around major releases. For staging access we request a scoped staging environment; for production tests we prefer a restricted read-only approach (no active exploits against prod).
- Evidence cadence: we typically deliver SOC 2 and supporting attestations once per quarter; for ad-hoc evidence requests we use a secure Drive share and aim for 3 business-day turnaround for standard logs and 5 business days for more complex requests.
- Limitations: we can provide sampled logs and configuration screenshots but do not provide ongoing remote access or direct queries against customer databases.

I've attached our current draft exhibit and a simple evidence-timetable template. Jordan — can you review the redline language below and suggest any legal constraints we should surface to NexaCare? Karthik — any technical caveats or minimum lead times we should call out?

Proposed next steps:
1) Jordan to post suggested exhibit redlines (1–2 business days)
2) Karthik to confirm acceptable pen-test windows + access limitations
3) We circulate a single-page exhibit and a proposed Aug/Sept test window for NexaCare to confirm

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v3.docx; evidence-timetable-template.xlsx

Thanks,

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: pen test window & evidence cadence

Soojin / Karthik — quick legal read and redline suggestions. I kept the language tight to avoid opening perpetual inspection rights. Main points:

- Inspection scope: propose replacing any "inspection" term with "limited evidence requests and sampling". Add a hard cap: one on-site or remote interactive inspection per 12-month period with 30-day notice.
- Lookback window: limit log/sample requests to the most recent 90 calendar days unless escalated (evidence older than 90 days requires additional legal approval).
- Response SLA: offer 3 business days for standard evidence requests (SOC reports, screenshots, sampled logs), 7 business days for requests requiring cross-team coordination.
- Pen test carve-outs: accept customer-conducted third-party pen tests with 30-day notice provided the test plan excludes destructive testing and any requirement for Redwood to provide credentials for remote execution. We should add explicit language: "Provider will not permit execution of arbitrary code or write operations against production systems as part of customer-led testing."
- Confidentiality & redaction: we will redact any customer-identifiable metrics and provide anonymized samples where appropriate.

Suggested exhibit snippet (to include under "Audit & Security Exhibit - Evidence Requests"):
"Provider shall respond to standard evidence requests within three (3) business days. Evidence requests shall be limited to sampled logs and configuration artifacts covering a maximum of ninety (90) calendar days, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Customer-led penetration tests require thirty (30) days' written notice and must not include destructive testing or require Provider to grant write or execution privileges against production systems."

Please confirm if we want to offer any concessions (e.g., one accelerated 2-business-day SLA for critical legal requests) — might be useful commercially. Also, we should surface any Deal-specific ask to Sales if NexaCare requests a persistent longer lookback or more frequent inspection.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Choi <emily.choi@nexacare.com>

Thanks — that language looks reasonable. NexaCare is comfortable with:

- 30-day notice for customer-led pen tests (we'll avoid destructive testing and won't request write/exec rights).
- 90-day lookback for sampled logs for standard requests.
- 3 business day turnaround for standard evidence; 7 days for cross-team items.

We'd like to target Aug 9–13 as our preferred pen-test window (internal scheduling permitting). Can Redwood confirm availability for that week, and share a DocuSign link for the updated order form / exhibit when ready? We'll run an internal tabletop the week prior and share any final constraints.

Attachments: NexaCare-pen-test-constraints.pdf (from earlier)

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — Emily
Emily Choi
